answer: Willow-cut clustering.** An agent earns standing only by routing traffic through distinct neighbors whose own paths stay separated near a willow root checkpoint, so clusters that grow too dense get pruned. Each identity must then sustain independent copper relay links across separate network regions to retain standing. To fake one identity, an attacker must provision and maintain distinct routes reaching a summit of sparse cut points, paying real bandwidth and latency per clone, which makes mass identity creation costlier than honest participation.
